title.narrative: Humanitarian Support: Improving Humanitarian Action - Syria Flexible Funds

description.narrative: Humanitarian support: Outcomes for crisis-affected populations are improved through agile, efficient and effective humanitarian assistance with identified strategic and emergent priorities: The programme, implemented by Save the Children in partnership with TAS and Violet, addresses urgent education, livelihoods and household-resilience needs among conflict-affected populations in Syria, including returnees, internally displaced people and host communities. In Idleb, SC and TAS will provide one-off multi-purpose cash transfers of USD 150 aligned with the Survival Minimum Expenditure Basket to help vulnerable families meet essential needs such as food, shelter and healthcare, while also delivering a mental health and psychosocial support session for children and caregivers to reduce distress, strengthen coping strategies and support smoother reintegration for returning children. In Aleppo, Violet will implement cash-for-work activities employing skilled and unskilled workers to rehabilitate ten schools and community facilities, prioritizing safe, inclusive and gender-sensitive upgrades such as improved sanitation, playgrounds and accessible infrastructure for children with disabilities. Schools will be selected with the Directorate of Education based on levels of displacement, return, and out-of-school children, and workers will be compensated based on locally assessed wage rates. To ensure sustainability and improved learning outcomes, Save the Children and Violet will also provide training to teachers in supported schools, strengthening their capacity to deliver quality, inclusive education that benefits all enrolled children and supports long-term system resilience. All SC programmes are gender mainstreamed, inclusive and aims to strengthen resilience.
